description: The plot illustrates how accuracy measures vary as a function of “Initial Confidence,” showing three series labeled Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy with vertical error bars. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” appears to use a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.86 to 1.00 with tick labels shown at 0.86, 0.88, and then at roughly 0.01 increments from 0.89 through 1.00. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with major ticks at 0.2 intervals. The Final Accuracy series is drawn as a blue solid line with circular markers and blue error bars; it stays high across the range, starting near about 0.92 at confidence 0.86 and ending near about 0.98 at 1.00, with values hovering around roughly 0.95–1.00 and reaching about 1.00 around 0.97–0.99. The Δ Accuracy series is an orange dashed line with diamond markers and orange error bars; it begins around 0.28–0.30 at 0.86, declines through the mid-range to around 0.05 near about 0.95, then increases again toward the right, reaching roughly 0.20 at 1.00, with a visible local bump around 0.92 near ~0.20. The Initial Accuracy series is shown as a green dashed line with square markers and green error bars; it starts around 0.64 at 0.86, generally rises to around 0.90–0.92 by about 0.94–0.96, and then trends downward at the far right, ending near about 0.77 at 1.00.
